ai.claude: The price gap says Google is betting on capability, not cost, at the low end; its own Search traffic absorbs the expense. For everyday work such as summarising site reports or tagging drawings, the cheapest models from Anthropic and OpenAI are now hard to beat; test Hydrogen only where its answers are clearly better.
ai.fact: Google launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen, its lowest-cost Gemini 4 model, at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens; it becomes the free-tier model and will power AI features in Google Search. Simon Willison notes that Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna cost $0.10 and $0.50, and that Google's larger Gemini 4 Carbon and Argon double in price to $4 and $20 on 1 December.

austrian.claude: The argument is consistent on its own terms, but suspending naturalisation would create a large permanent class of residents without political rights, which sits poorly with liberty. Switzerland is a partial test: tight naturalisation and residence-based rules have not stopped high immigration, because the labour market keeps demanding it.
austrian.fact: As President Trump threatens to double tariffs on Mexico over a migrant caravan and Spain faces a crisis at its Ceuta border, the Mises Institute's Ryan McMaken published three free-market ways to reduce immigration.

opinion.text: proposes suspending all naturalisation, cutting off welfare for migrants and abolishing anti-discrimination laws, so that migration is limited by what the market and private property owners accept, while the state shrinks.

src.t: Mises Institute: Three Free-Market Ways to Limit Immigration

top.claude: A system-wide halt from a communications fault, not an attack, is the worrying part: it suggests the US air-traffic network has too few fallbacks. Expect the episode to feed the long-running fight in Congress over funding to modernise the FAA's ageing equipment.
top.fact: The FAA stopped all flights across the United States on Friday, citing extraordinary circumstances and safety, after communication problems at air-traffic control centres. Officials said no threat had been detected. Flights resumed after a stop of several hours, but passengers still faced delays and cancellations on Saturday, and the FAA has not yet published a full cause.

top.claude: The weekly close on Sunday night matters more than one evening's price, since weekend trading is thin. The bigger driver is outside crypto: as long as the dollar and bond yields keep rising, Bitcoin trades like a leveraged bet on liquidity, not as a safe haven.
top.fact: Bitcoin traded around $65,400 on Saturday evening, down about 4.5% in 24 hours and roughly 14% over seven days, according to CoinGecko. It is the sixth weekly loss in a row. The fall comes as the dollar strengthens, US 10-year yields stay above 5% and the AI trade wobbles after Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia.

opinion.text: argues that $66,000 is the trendline that has held Bitcoin up for three years; losing it opens a move below $50,000 and could extend the bear market by a year, even though long-term valuations look historically cheap.

top.fact: A global Microsoft outage on Friday disrupted Outlook, Teams and other Microsoft 365 services, and swissinfo reported that Swiss businesses and public authorities were affected. Microsoft said services were recovering during the day while some disruptions continued.

top.claude: Turkey already has a military base in Qatar, so a pact would formalise an existing tie rather than create a new alliance. The NPT debate is the more serious signal: Iranian MPs have threatened this before as leverage, but a formal exit would make new Israeli or US strikes far more likely.
top.fact: President Trump said on Thursday that the US does not need a deal with Iran, ending talks Gulf states had backed. On Friday, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan hosted Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani in Istanbul, where the two signed new agreements.
